name: Aurora oval — Scandinavia/Baltic
notes: Aurora + Baltic city lights at the edge of ISS lat reach. Strongest single category for solar-cycle-peak imagery.
caption_hook: Aurora arc with Stockholm/Helsinki/St Petersburg city lights below — solar wind hitting the upper atmosphere while people sleep underneath

name: Aurora oval — Canada/northern US oblique
notes: Yellowknife/Edmonton/Winnipeg corridor; oblique to the north. Pair with NOAA SWPC 30-min forecast.

name: Aurora oval — south of Australia/NZ
notes: Antarctic aurora visible at Tasmania/NZ obliques. Underrepresented in social feeds — high engagement opportunity.

name: Aurora oval — Patagonia
notes: Tierra del Fuego + Andes silhouette + aurora. Rare composition.

name: Aurora oval — South Atlantic / Southern Ocean
notes: Pure aurora over open ocean; works with airglow + Earth limb.

name: US East Coast corridor (Boston-NY-Philly-DC)
notes: Densest urban corridor in N America; coastline visible.
caption_hook: From Boston to DC at night — 50 million people, one continuous glow tracing the Atlantic coast

name: Chicago / Great Lakes / Detroit / Toronto
notes: Chicago + the Great Lakes outline is one of the most recognizable night shapes from orbit.
caption_hook: Chicago burning bright on the lake's southern tip; the Great Lakes carved out as black voids

name: Florida / Cuba / Bahamas at night
notes: Iconic three-island geometry; works with moonglint on water.
caption_hook: Florida, Cuba, and the Bahamas under moonlight. City lights trace where people live; moonglint traces the sea. Can you find your city?

name: Los Angeles / San Diego / Tijuana
notes: Border-city contrast (US grid vs Mexican grid pattern is visible).

name: San Francisco Bay at night
notes: Bay shape + bridges + Silicon Valley tech corridor.

name: Las Vegas at night
notes: Brightest single point per capita on Earth — visually unmistakable.

name: Texas Triangle (Dallas–Houston–San Antonio–Austin)
notes: Four-corner mega-region; gulf coast curve in same frame.

name: Mexico City
notes: World's largest contiguous urban-light footprint at night per area.

name: São Paulo / Rio corridor
notes: Two megacities + Atlantic coast in one frame.

name: Buenos Aires / Montevideo
notes: Río de la Plata is one of the world's widest river mouths — strong outline.

name: London / Benelux / Paris (oblique)
notes: At ISS lat-limit; oblique passes only. Densest European night-light cluster.

name: Italy at night (boot-shaped lights)
notes: Most recognizable European country shape; lit edges show the boot.
caption_hook: Italy at night — the boot draws itself in city lights, kicking Sicily across the Mediterranean

name: Nile Delta / Cairo / Suez
notes: NASA's most-cited 'people + geography' frame: Nile valley line + delta fan + Cairo + Suez + Red Sea entrance + Israel coast.
caption_hook: The Nile at night — 5,000 years of settlement laid out in a single ribbon of light, fanning into the delta and bottlenecking past Cairo

name: Persian Gulf — Dubai / Doha / Kuwait
notes: Gulf coastline + Palm Jumeirah outline + oil flares + multiple country grids in one shot.

name: India megaregion — Delhi / Mumbai / Kolkata / Dhaka
notes: Indo-Gangetic plain glow + Bay of Bengal coastline + Himalayas to north.

name: Tokyo / Osaka / Nagoya megalopolis
notes: World's largest contiguous metro lights; coastline + bay shapes.

name: Korean Peninsula at night (DMZ visible)
notes: Lit South vs dark North — the most viscerally readable political boundary in any orbital photo.
caption_hook: The Korean peninsula at night — South Korea blazes; the DMZ is visible as a sudden cliff into darkness

name: Shanghai / Yangtze River Delta
notes: Yangtze delta lit + city outline of Shanghai + East China Sea coast.

name: Pearl River Delta — Hong Kong / Shenzhen / Guangzhou / Macau
notes: Densest urban-light cluster in southern China; islands + bridges visible.

name: Singapore / Malacca Strait
notes: Equatorial; Singapore + Sumatra coast + ship lights in the strait.

name: Italy + Sicily (daylight, recognizable shape)
notes: Day-side counterpart to Italy-night. Sicily + Etna in same frame.

name: Baja California / Gulf of California
notes: Striking contrast: red desert + turquoise gulf + Pacific cold ocean.

name: Red Sea / Sinai / Saudi coast
notes: Tectonic rift visible as a perfectly straight gulf.

name: Caribbean island arc
notes: Dotted line of islands from Trinidad to Cuba; reef colors.

name: New Zealand
notes: Two-island silhouette + Southern Alps spine.

name: Iberian peninsula + Strait of Gibraltar
notes: 8-mile gap between two continents — Strait of Gibraltar in a single frame.

name: Madagascar
notes: Distinctive elongated island; deforestation patterns visible.

name: Himalayas / Karakoram / Tibetan Plateau
notes: Highest range on Earth; snow + lake plateau contrast.
caption_hook: The roof of the world — Everest, K2, and the highest plateau on Earth, snow-bright against the brown Indian plain

name: Andes / Patagonian glaciers
notes: Glaciers + fjords + ice fields; high visual contrast at any sun angle.

name: Grand Canyon / Colorado Plateau
notes: Best at low sun angle for shadow detail.

name: Richat Structure (Eye of the Sahara)
notes: Geological bullseye; visible from any orbit, almost always cloud-free.

name: Namib Desert / Skeleton Coast
notes: Red dunes meeting cold Atlantic — one of the highest-contrast Earth images possible.

name: Atacama Desert / Salar de Atacama
notes: Salar + lithium-mining ponds visible as colored squares.

name: Amazon River bends + tributaries
notes: Oxbows + meanders + Rio Negro/Solimões black-and-tan confluence.

name: Okavango Delta
notes: Inland river delta in the middle of Kalahari — green fan in dry land.

name: Great Barrier Reef
notes: Best at sun-glint geometry for reef structure.

name: Bahamas banks
notes: Iconic turquoise sandbars + tiger-stripe tidal patterns.

name: Hawaiian Islands chain
notes: Volcanic chain + Honolulu lights at night + Mauna Loa snow possible.

name: Iceland
notes: Northernmost reach (oblique only); volcanoes + glaciers + black sand.

name: Norwegian fjords
notes: Edge of ISS lat range; oblique only.

name: Salar de Uyuni
notes: World's largest salt flat; mirror finish when wet.

name: Mt. Etna, Sicily
notes: Active; plume often visible. Best at terminator.

name: Stromboli
notes: Continuous mild eruptions; lava glow at night.

name: Vesuvius / Campi Flegrei (Naples)
notes: Naples in same frame; geological context.

name: Kīlauea, Hawaii
notes: Lava glow at night is unmistakable.

name: Popocatépetl, Mexico
notes: Mexico City in same frame for context.

name: Volcán de Fuego, Guatemala
notes: Frequent ash plumes.

name: Taal Volcano, Philippines
notes: Crater lake within crater — one of the most photogenic volcano shapes.

name: Klyuchevskoy / Kamchatka volcano chain
notes: Chain of 30+ volcanoes; world's most active region per area.

name: Mt. Fuji
notes: Best with clear skies + snow cap.

name: Catatumbo lightning, Lake Maracaibo
notes: World's most concentrated lightning; ~280 strikes/hour during peak.

name: Lightning capital — Congo basin
notes: Highest annual lightning density on Earth; storms most active afternoon-to-night UTC.

name: Lightning belt — Maritime Continent
notes: Indonesia + Malaysia + Borneo storm cells; afternoon convection peak.

name: Lightning belt — Pacific ITCZ
notes: Storm cells frequent; lightning + airglow + Earth limb composition.

name: Atlantic hurricane basin (when active)
notes: Active June-November. Photograph with public-awareness caption, not as spectacle.

Victoria Falls / Lake Kariba
notes: Plume of mist visible from orbit.

name: Lake Natron, Tanzania
notes: Red alkaline waters.

name: Betsiboka River delta, Madagascar
notes: Red sediment plumes from deforestation; vivid post-rain.

name: Great Salt Lake (daylight)
notes: Pink/purple split by causeway.
